subject: Biology
description: Glycolysis, Krebs cycle, electron transport chain, ATP yield, aerobic vs anaerobic

questions.stem: The MITOCHONDRION is often called the 'powerhouse' of the cell because it:

options.option_text: Stores all the genetic material of the cell
Produces most of the cell's ATP through respiration
Synthesises proteins from amino acids inside it
Filters out waste from the cell's interior

questions.explanation: Mitochondrion — site of aerobic cellular respiration. Houses the Krebs cycle (matrix) + Electron Transport Chain (inner membrane). Produces ~30-32 ATP per glucose via oxidative phosphorylation. Has its own circular DNA + ribosomes (endosymbiotic origin from ancient α-proteobacteria, ~2 billion years ago). Distractor 1 = nucleus. Distractor 3 = ribosomes (in cytoplasm + RER). Distractor 4 = lysosomes / kidney role.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: GLYCOLYSIS, the first stage of cellular respiration, takes place in the:

options.option_text: Mitochondrial matrix, deep inside the organelle
Cytoplasm of the cell, outside the mitochondria
Inner mitochondrial membrane, with the ETC
Endoplasmic reticulum, attached to ribosomes

questions.explanation: GLYCOLYSIS — Greek 'glyco' (sugar) + 'lysis' (splitting). Glucose (6 C) → 2 pyruvate (3 C each). 10-step pathway, ALL in the cytoplasm. Net yield: 2 ATP + 2 NADH per glucose. Does NOT need O₂ → can run in anaerobic conditions. PYRUVATE FATE: aerobic → enters mitochondria → Krebs cycle. Anaerobic → fermentation: lactic acid (in muscles, yogurt bacteria) or ethanol + CO₂ (in yeast).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The KREBS CYCLE (TCA / Citric Acid cycle) takes place in the:

options.option_text: Cytoplasm of the cell, outside the mitochondria
Mitochondrial matrix, the innermost compartment
Inner mitochondrial membrane (with the ETC)
Outer mitochondrial membrane facing the cytoplasm

questions.explanation: KREBS / Citric Acid / TCA cycle — site: mitochondrial MATRIX. Acetyl-CoA (2 C, from pyruvate decarboxylation) + oxaloacetate (4 C) → citrate (6 C) → series of reactions → back to oxaloacetate. Per acetyl-CoA: 3 NADH + 1 FADH₂ + 1 GTP (≈ATP) + 2 CO₂. Glucose makes 2 pyruvate → 2 acetyl-CoA → 2 cycles. Discovered by Sir Hans Krebs (Nobel 1953). Distractor 1 = glycolysis. Distractor 3 = ETC site. Distractor 4 = nothing important happens there.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: AEROBIC respiration of one glucose molecule produces approximately how many ATP?

options.option_text: 2 ATP, the same as anaerobic glycolysis output
30-32 ATP, including all stages of respiration
100 ATP, much more than the actual yield
Zero — glucose alone produces no ATP at all

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration: ~30-32 ATP / glucose total. Breakdown: GLYCOLYSIS — 2 ATP + 2 NADH; pyruvate → acetyl-CoA — 2 NADH; KREBS — 6 NADH + 2 FADH₂ + 2 GTP; OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION — converts NADH (~2.5 ATP) and FADH₂ (~1.5 ATP) into bulk ATP via electron transport chain + chemiosmosis (Peter Mitchell, Nobel 1978). Anaerobic glycolysis alone — only 2 ATP/glucose (much less efficient). Distractor 1 = glycolysis only. Distractor 3 too high. Distractor 4 false.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: During strenuous exercise, muscles can produce energy ANAEROBICALLY, generating which by-product that causes muscle fatigue?

options.option_text: Ethanol, found in alcoholic fermentation
Lactic acid, accumulating in skeletal muscle cells
Carbon dioxide, exhaled rapidly during exertion
Oxygen, which then gets stored in muscles

questions.explanation: When O₂ supply lags demand during heavy exercise, pyruvate is reduced to LACTIC ACID (lactate fermentation) by lactate dehydrogenase. Regenerates NAD⁺ to keep glycolysis running short-term. Lactic acid accumulation in muscles → soreness + fatigue. After exercise, lactate transported to liver → reconverted to glucose (Cori cycle). YEASTS use ethanol fermentation instead → ethanol + CO₂ (the basis of beer, wine, bread rising). Distractor 3 — CO₂ is from aerobic respiration. Distractor 4 — opposite of how O₂ works.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The OVERALL equation for aerobic respiration of glucose can be summarised as:

options.option_text: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6H₂O → 6CO₂ + 6O₂ + ATP
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + ATP
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (sugar made)
C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2 lactic acid + 2 ATP only

questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration overall: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + ~30-32 ATP. Glucose oxidised to CO₂ and water, releasing energy captured as ATP. Distractor 3 = PHOTOSYNTHESIS (the reverse, plants make sugar). Distractor 4 = anaerobic respiration / lactate fermentation (only 2 ATP). Distractor 1 — wrong reactants/products.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: FERMENTATION in BREAD-MAKING relies on yeast cells that:

options.option_text: Convert flour into pure carbon dioxide gas alone
Break down sugars into ethanol and CO₂, leavening the dough
Polymerise starch into long chains making the dough rise
Photosynthesise inside the dough using oven-light energy

questions.explanation: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's/brewer's yeast) — ferments sugars (from starch breakdown by amylases in flour) into ETHANOL + CO₂ (alcoholic fermentation). CO₂ bubbles get trapped in the gluten network → bread rises. Ethanol evaporates during baking. Same yeast in beer/wine — alcohol stays. WINE — fruit sugars in grapes; BEER — malted barley sugars; BREAD — flour sugars. Distractor 1 — ethanol is also produced. Distractor 3 — wrong process. Distractor 4 — yeast is heterotrophic, doesn't photosynthesise.
